title: Protocol for the generation and automated confocal imaging of whole multi-cellular tumor spheroids
protocol: Pre-warm culture medium to 37°C before thawing cells.
Remove cells from cryogenic storage and place the vial into a 37°C water bath.
Transport cells on ice in an appropriately isolated container to avoid premature defrosting.
Defrost cells in the water bath.
Gently swirl the vial during defrosting until there is a small particle of ice remaining.
Spray the vial with ethanol to sterilize it.
Transfer the contents to 5 mL of warm serum medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube at 3 min, 300 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of culture medium.
Transfer the resuspended cells into a culture flask containing 10–15 mL culture medium.
Allow 2–3 passages of cells prior to performing experiments with them.
Pre-warm 1× PBS without Calcium and Magnesium to 37°C.
Pre-warm culture media for the cell type to 37°C.
Pre-warm Trypsin-EDTA to 37°C.
Remove culture media from cells.
Wash cells twice with pre-warmed PBS (5 mL).
Incubate 5 mL of Trypsin-EDTA per T75 flask for up to 5 minutes to detach cells.
Quench Trypsin-EDTA using an equal volume of culture medium (5 mL).
Pellet cells at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and re-suspend cells in 5 mL of culture medium.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension to 15 mL of cell culture media in a fresh T75 flask.
Confirm presence of cells via visual inspection under a bench-top microscope.
Place flask into the incubator.
Pre-warm 1× PBS to 37°C.
Pre-warm culture media for each cell type to 37°C.
Pre-warm Spheroid Culture Medium to 37°C.
Pre-warm Trypsin-EDTA to 37°C.
Remove culture media from cells and wash twice with 5 mL of pre-warmed PBS.
Incubate 5 mL of Trypsin-EDTA per T75 flask for up to 5 min to detach cells.
Visually confirm detachment under a bench-top microscope (10× objective).
Quench Trypsin-EDTA using an equal volume of culture medium (5 mL).
Pellet cells (3 min, 300 × g).
Discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend cells in 5 mL of culture medium.
Pass suspension through an 18-gauge blunt-ended needle.
Determine viable cell count using a hemocytometer with trypan blue staining.
Prepare enough cells for 100 wells by adding the appropriate volumes of fibroblasts, cancer cells, and spheroid culture medium to a falcon tube.
Gently mix by inverting the tube three times.
Add 150 μL of cell suspension to each well of an ultra-low attachment plate.
Centrifuge the plate for 5 minutes at 300 × g.
Incubate plate under culturing conditions for 3–6 days.
Harvest spheroids by gently pipetting the media up and down in each well.
Collect desired number of spheroids (up to 10) in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Transfer harvested spheroids to Ibidi chamber slide for further analysis or imaging.
Use a 1000 μL pipette tip to prevent shearing of the spheroids during transfer.
Centrifuge the spheroids for a short pulse of 10 seconds at low g (e.g., 20 × g).
Aspirate the supernatant carefully, leaving 50–150 μl residual media in the Eppendorf tube to avoid discarding any spheroids.
Transfer the contents of one Eppendorf tube including the spheroids into a well of an 8-well chamber slide (Ibidi).
Ensure that the well bottom and all spheroids are fully covered with medium.
Add additional media as needed to cover the spheroids.
Mix equal volumes of 2× neutralized Collagen I solution to the residual media.
Prepare and store the 2× Collagen solutions on ice to prevent premature setting.
Work quickly to transfer spheroids into the chamber slide after mixing collagen with residual media.
Do not exceed a total transfer volume of 150 μL per well, given that each well has a working volume of 300 μL.
Let collagen set for 1 hour under culturing conditions before proceeding.
Add 100 μL of culture media to the set collagen and incubate as desired.
Allow the spheroids to attach for 8–16 h.
Proceed to fixation and staining steps after attachment is complete.
Permeabilize spheroids with TX-100.
Stain spheroids using antibodies against the desired target.
Clear and refractive index-match spheroids prior to imaging.
Aspirate culture medium from each well of the chamber slide.
Wash spheroids twice with 250 μL of 1× PBS.
Fix spheroids using 250 μL/well of pre-warmed (37°C) 4% PFA for 1 h at room temperature.
Remove PFA and quench residual PFA with 0.1M Tris/HCl (pH = 8) for 30 min at room temperature.
Permeabilize spheroids using 200 μL/well of 1% TX-100 for 3 h at room temperature.
Block unspecific protein binding using 200 μL/well of blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate with 250 μL/well of the primary antibody (1:1000) diluted in the antibody dilution buffer for 40 h at 37°C.
Wash three times with 250 μL/well 0.5% TX-100 per well for 30 min at room temperature (1.5 h total).
Incubate 250 μL/well of the matching secondary antibody (1:1000) diluted in the antibody dilution buffer for at least 16 h at 37°C.
Wash three times with 250 μL 0.5% TX-100/well for 30 min at room temperature.
Incubate with 150 μL/well of a 1:500 dilution of the primary antibody for 40 h (collagen).
Wash four times with 100 μL 0.5% TX-100/well for 1 h (4 h total, collagen).
Incubate 150 μL/well of a 1:500 dilution of the secondary antibody for 16 h (collagen).
Wash collagen four times with 100 μL of 0.5% TX-100 per well for 1 hour (total wash time is 4 hours).
Counterstain with 150 μL/well of Hoechst33432 at a ratio of 1:1000 and add ActinRed to the solution.
Incubate with 150 μL/well of pre-warmed optical clearing media (RI = 1.46 at room temperature) for 1 hour at 37°C.
Repeat step involving washing collagen with TX-100 three times.
Proceed to imaging.
Store samples at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Acclimatize the sample to the temperature of the imaging room for at least 30 min.
Start the microscope and mount your sample.
Turn on microscope, lasers, detectors, and other equipment.
Select a 10× far-working-distance objective (HC PL APO CS2 10x/0.40 DRY).
Insert your sample into the stage.
Find and focus on a random spheroid using the eyepieces of your microscope and transmitted light.
Set up the laser emission and detector gain for the nuclear channel as instructed.
Adjust imaging settings for Leica microscope: set resolution to 256 × 256 pixels and bidirectional scanning on.
Widen pinhole to increase optical section thickness (Pinhole = 113.3 μm, Pinhole Airy = 2 AU).
Use digital zoom of 0.7× (not recommended for detailed imaging).
Find and focus on the middle of a random spheroid.
Repeat focusing procedure for several spheroids in multiple wells and record z-focus levels.
Average recorded focus levels and set to this average level.
Image the whole plate using stage-based navigation tool.
Change objective to 20× immersion objective with sufficient working distance.
Lower 10× objective to the lowest height possible.
Select the 20× glycerol immersion objective.
Add a drop of glycerol immersion fluid (RI = 1.47 at RT) onto the objective (HC PL APO CORR CS2 20x/0.75 IMM, FWD: 0.66 mm).
Adjust correction collar to match the immersion fluid if required.
Coat the bottom of the chamber slide with a thin film of glycerol.
Place the sample in the stage.
Check the orientation of the chamber slide to ensure it is placed correctly according to the plate map.
If no glycerol-compatible immersion objective is available, use an alternative objective with a far-working range.
Adjust the height of the objective until the immersion fluid touches the bottom of the slide.
Move to eyepieces and focus on the sample.
View cells in every channel necessary for the fluorophores in the sample.
Adjust detector gain and laser power to minimize oversaturated pixels while enabling full intensity range.
Enable sequential scan between frames to avoid bleed through of fluorophores.
Open the plate image in the stage-based navigation tool and select the regions of interest for imaging.
Start the imaging.
